expectations.text: Notes that 4% is small/typical and not immediately alarming
expectations.evidence: Response states: '~4% is within the normal range for HB reversals and is almost certainly not a problem requiring immediate action.' Also: 'At 4%, this is well within the 1–5% range that is statistically expected from sparse individual data, not from genuine conspicuous-consumption preferences. It is not a sign that the design or estimation broke.'

expectations.text: Does NOT default to constraining monotonicity as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly advises against constraining: 'Do not reflexively constrain monotonicity' in the short answer, and in the dedicated section: 'The practical recommendation at 4%: Do not constrain.' Constraining is listed last in the checklist (step 5) and only recommended above 10–15%.

expectations.text: Presents at least two of three options: leave alone / constrain / investigate
expectations.evidence: All three options are covered. 'Leave alone' is recommended for Category 1 shrinkage artifacts ('the reversals are artifacts — leave them alone'). 'Investigate' is the first step ('Don't assume the reversals are all noise. They fall into three categories...'). 'Constrain' is discussed in the 'On constraining monotonicity' section with explicit tradeoffs.

expectations.text: Mentions HB shrinkage toward population mean as a plausible cause of reversals
expectations.evidence: Response devotes a full section to this: 'HB shrinks each respondent's individual utility vector toward the population mean. Respondents who provided limited information... get pulled hard toward the group center. The shrinkage is asymmetric: a respondent who was mildly price-sensitive in their actual choices can end up with a slightly positive price slope after shrinkage, purely because the population mean for price is near zero and the individual data doesn't overwhelm it.'

claims.claim: 1–5% reversal range is called out explicitly in the skill reference (hb-estimation.md)
claims.evidence: Transcript confirms: 'reversals are an artifact of HB shrinkage + sparse individual data at 1–5%; three options enumerated (leave alone, impose monotonicity, investigate)'

claims.claim: The practical threshold for constraining is ~10–15%
claims.evidence: Response states: 'If this were 15–20%, the calculus shifts.' Checklist step 5: 'Do not constrain monotonicity unless the reversal rate climbs above ~10–15%.'

claims.claim: Posterior draws vs. posterior means advice is provided for simulations
claims.evidence: Response advises: 'run your simulation on full posterior draws (not just posterior means). Respondents with reversed price utilities who are genuinely uncertain (wide posteriors) will contribute less extreme values in the simulation because their uncertainty is propagated.'

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks whether the response correctly distinguishes between shrinkage artifacts vs. genuine heterogeneity vs. data quality issues as separate diagnostic categories — the three-category framework is a core piece of skill guidance and a wrong answer could still pass by mentioning 'investigate' generically without any structure.

suggestions.assertion: Presents at least two of three options: leave alone / constrain / investigate
suggestions.reason: This assertion is satisfied even if the response recommended constraining as the primary action but also mentioned the other two options briefly. The more meaningful check is whether 'constrain' is NOT the primary recommendation — which is already covered by expectation 2. Consider merging or narrowing expectation 3 to avoid redundancy.

eval_feedback.overall: The four assertions cover the key behaviors well and all pass with clear evidence. The main gap is that no assertion checks the structural quality of the diagnostic reasoning (three-category framework vs. generic 'investigate' advice), which would better discriminate a skill-informed response from a generally informed one.
